title: Coconut cream truffles
subtitle: white chocolate and coconut ganache truffles rolled in desiccated coconut
excerpt: Coconut cream truffles use coconut cream in place of dairy cream to make the ganache, giving them a clean, tropical flavour with no added dairy. The ganache is white chocolate based, which lets the coconut come through without competition. Rolled in desiccated coconut, they look like snowballs.
sourceNotes: Coconut cream truffle, a standard dairy-free confectionery variant; coconut-white chocolate ganache method from modern British patisserie practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The thick, fat-rich liquid pressed from fresh coconut flesh. Higher in fat and richer than coconut milk, and used in truffles as a direct replacement for double cream.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncoated in a single layer. Defrost overnight in the fridge and roll in desiccated coconut before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 10 days.

content.text: Place the finely chopped white chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat the coconut cream in a small saucepan over a medium heat until it just comes to a simmer, then pour it over the chocolate.

Leave for 2 minutes, then stir from the centre outward until smooth. Add the vanilla extract and stir to combine. White chocolate is sweeter and more sensitive to heat than dark; stir gently and do not apply further heat if the ganache looks lumpy; the residual warmth will dissolve any remaining pieces.
Cover with cling film pressed onto the surface and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until firm.

Spread the desiccated coconut on a plate. Scoop pieces of chilled ganache roughly 2 cm across and roll quickly between your palms into balls. White chocolate ganache is softer and warms faster than dark, so work in small batches and refrigerate the remaining ganache between batches.
Roll each ball in the desiccated coconut until fully coated. Transfer to a tray and refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving.

attrs.problem: Ganache too soft to roll even after chilling
attrs.avoid: Avoid using coconut milk instead of coconut cream; the lower fat content gives a soft ganache that may not firm.
attrs.fix: Place the bowl in the freezer for 20 minutes, then try scooping again.

attrs.problem: White chocolate ganache seizes and turns grainy
attrs.avoid: Avoid overheating the coconut cream; a hard boil can split white chocolate instantly.
attrs.fix: Heat the coconut cream only to a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil.
